summary_paragraph: A 68-year-old woman was admitted with acute on chronic diastolic heart failure, presenting with bilateral leg swelling, dyspnea, weight gain, and pink-tinged sputum. She was found to have worsening atelectasis and imaging findings suggestive of pneumonia, for which she received antibiotics. A new right seventh rib fracture was identified, likely contributing to pleuritic pain. Acute kidney injury developed on the background of chronic kidney disease but improved with careful diuresis. Her immune thrombocytopenia remained stable without intervention. Over 12 days, she responded well to treatment, with resolution of respiratory symptoms, improved oxygenation, and stable renal function. She was discharged home with a plan for close outpatient follow-up.
